messages.author: f84c6e98f30fb228
messages.subject: index of association
parts:
Hi,

Please help in calculating the index of association from vcf files.
I have 5 gene locus for 30 samples ( 30 vcf files for each gene).
I am not able to understand how can I use 30 files to calculate IA. Do I need to merge the 30 vcf file for each gene.

Any kind of help will be appreciated.


Thanks!

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] index of association
parts:
Hello,

You should be able to represent all your data in a single VCF file. I believe the `vcf-concat` program from the vcftools suite should be able to concatenate your vcf files for you.

From there, you can use the vcfR package to read your data into R and use the vcfR2genind() function to convert your data to a genind object. From there, you can calculate the index of association on your data.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

messages.author: 251f569434b3da1e
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] index of association
parts:
Hello, I think a relevant question is why do you have your data organized into separate files? If you have *g.vcf files created by the GATK's haplotype caller than you should run their GenotypeGVCF (https://software.broadinstitute.org/gatk/documentation/tooldocs/3.8-0/org_broadinstitute_gatk_tools_walkers_variantutils_GenotypeGVCFs.php) on them to create one file. If this is not the case then I think you should consider recalling your variants in a manner that results in one file. The VCF file will only have information on the variable positions. So if a position was variable in one individual but not in another that second one will have no information for that position. If you call variants over all your samples at once the variant caller should provide information on invariant sites (homozygous for the reference allele) if the position is variable in one of the other samples.

Good luck!
Brian

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] index of association
parts:
Hi,

In general, a high p-value of the index of association will indicate that you failed to reject the null hypothesis of unlinked loci in your population based on this test of multilocus linkage.

That being said, the documentation for ia has several relevant resources. I would recommend reading Agapow and Burt, 2001; and Smith et al. 1993 for details and caveats. Additionally, you may want to peruse the fifth chapter of my dissertation, which explores the limitations of this index and contains more references: https://zkamvar.github.io/dissertation/5-factors-influencing-inference-of-clonality-in-diploid-populations.html 

Best,
Zhian
